title: No-op post hooks repeat inspection before suppressing duplicate feedback
symptom: Two consecutive post hooks on the same captured 135-file, 4675-group candidate took 19.959 and 30.810 seconds. The second response was empty JSON, but detector work was repeated. A spy reproduction observed one inspect callback per unchanged post and a fresh callback on Stop.

rootCause.summary: Original 2026-11-14 mechanism, superseded in the local 2026-11-16 candidate: The lifecycle hook compares current content with the original session baseline and inspects all changed supported files before claiming the feedback marker. The marker suppresses duplicate output, not source analysis. No result cache is present. TypeScript loading opens and closes a fresh API server per file; closing it is an existing resource-safety boundary.

requestedOutcome: Bound repeated no-op post-hook cost while preserving complete session-change coverage, refusal reporting, source-race checks, effective-context invalidation and a complete read-only Stop check.
decisions: Record this as a measured performance mechanism, not an established safety bug or permission to disable hooks.
Do not reset the baseline after commit, weaken source checks or remove TypeScript server cleanup.

At the initial 2026-11-14 observation: A possible post-result cache must bind content, canonical path, mode, effective config, proof/rule documents and engine/runtime/parser/project inputs, with before/after race checks. Stop may conservatively bypass such a cache. This is a proposal, not implemented behavior.
The staging environment omitted the original full dependency/baseline environment and did not control concurrent load; the two measurements are not universal latency predictions.

actions.description: Preserve unchanged-input timing, inspect-call counts and source-control-flow evidence.
Design an explicit inspection-context identity and cache invalidation matrix before changing lifecycle code.
If implemented, verify no-op reuse, every context/source invalidation, races, refusal reporting and complete Stop coverage on isolated artifacts.

history.summary: Read-only and unchanged-input tools incurred repeated lifecycle latency.
The second post still inspected the same candidate before returning empty JSON; Stop independently inspected it as intended.
Retain the safety checks and classify context-complete cache work as unimplemented until regression and artifact evidence exists.
Implemented and locally verified the bounded issue63 correction; retained earlier consumer failures and unrun delivery/host limits.
